solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Such old salts initially saw in me, joining Navy?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word saw

parts.note: hip means fashionable, the same as in

explanation.surface: Someone muses that sailors of old would see themselves in the speaker, if the speaker joined the Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' makes the definition refer back to the old salts: sailors of a bygone era.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for seamen or sailors, which old salts are.

clue.text: The yacht ad Times cut out given to splitters?

indicators.note: cut tells us letters are removed and out tells us the remainder is rearranged

parts.note: T stands for time, so two of them give times

explanation.surface: A newspaper advertisement for a yacht is cut from the Times and given to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the two Ts (Times) from THE YACHT AD and rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A splitter is a splitting headache, so someone prone to them suffers from aching heads.

clue.text: Open ripe exotic Italian food

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are put in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Instructions to open some ripe, unusual Italian produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Italian sausage, familiar as a pizza topping.

clue.text: Bombs without G & T, perhaps?

parts.note: ex is a Latin preposition meaning out of or without, as in ex dividend
G and T are examples of plosive consonants, sounds made by stopping then releasing breath

explanation.surface: A party disaster: the drinks run out, no gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G & T' looks like gin and tonic; it is the letters G and T as speech sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombs are devices packed with material designed to blow up.

clue.text: Dope at work with Boris?

parts.note: in, as in 'in the office', means at work
Boris Johnson was then Foreign Secretary, heading the Foreign Office, FO

explanation.surface: A question whether someone foolish is working alongside Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: When this puzzle appeared Boris Johnson was the UK's Foreign Secretary, in charge of the Foreign Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information or facts.

clue.text: Forward painter's formal attire?

parts.note: the bow is the forward end of a boat
a painter is a rope that ties a boat up, so a tie

explanation.surface: An avant-garde artist's evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' is not an artist but a mooring rope; a forward painter is tied at the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckwear knot worn with a dinner jacket at black-tie events.

clue.text: Filipino dog clearly hasn't done the easiest thing!

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tag along

parts.words: clearly hasn't done the easiest thing
parts.note: the easiest thing is falling off a log; a log still in place clearly hasn't fallen off

explanation.surface: A dog from the Philippines that somehow fails at the simplest task.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry TAG sits on top of A LOG, which has not done the easiest thing: 'as easy as falling off a log'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main language of the Philippines, so a Filipino tongue.

clue.text: Settled in Rye — awful truth

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
awful suggests the word Rye is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to land or settle

explanation.surface: Someone who moved to the town of Rye learns a dreadful fact.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a small town in East Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is what actually is so, the same idea as truth.

clue.text: Facetiously give a hand behind pub to introduce something new

indicators.note: behind places the applause word after the pub in the answer

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ovate is a jokey verb made from ovation, to applaud

explanation.surface: Clapping at the back of a pub to launch something new.
explanation.walkthrough: OVATE is not a real verb meaning to applaud, hence 'Facetiously'.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to bring in new methods or ideas.

clue.text: Silver Knight's backer in stand? One sounds full of wind

indicators.note: in tells us the silver and backer go inside

parts.note: to stand is to be, to exist
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Gladys Knight was backed by the Pips, so one Pip is a Knight's backer

explanation.surface: A silver-coated knight's supporter blows loudly at a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knight is soul singer Gladys Knight, whose backing group was the Pips.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind instrument that sounds from a bag kept inflated with air.

clue.text: Flab lost playing this?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are put into play and moved about

explanation.surface: Lose weight by taking up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: playing this bat-and-ball game might lose you flab.
explanation.definitionFit: A game like baseball played with a larger ball, good exercise.

clue.text: Wily chap is about to reverse current, so I make my way through marshland

definitions.text: so I make my way through marshland
definitions.note: an adverb phrase: 'so' asks how I walk through the bog, as an adverb would

indicators.note: about tells us the sly word goes round the others

parts.note: a wily chap is sly
to quash a verdict is to reverse it
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A cunning man about to switch current while trudging through a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse current' looks like electricity; QUASH means reverse a decision and I alone is current.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in wet marsh, one moves with a soggy squelching sound underfoot.

clue.text: One should get tough about one's first shock treatment

indicators.note: about tells us the tough word is wrapped round the one

parts.note: hard means tough
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of one's

explanation.surface: A hard-line view that someone deserves electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a mass of hair, so shock treatment is styling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is what a shock of hair gets from a stylist.

clue.text: Even score with England captain: one for one?

parts.note: to square a score is to level it
Joe Root was then captain of England's cricket team

explanation.surface: England's captain levels the match, single-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: the square root of one is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A number that multiplied by itself gives the original; for one that is one.

clue.text: Transport company upset royal with reproach

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the company name upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Uber is a ride-hailing transport company
kingly means royal

explanation.surface: A taxi firm angers a royal by criticising them.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb describing speech that scolds or censures, done with reproach.

clue.text: That time on M1, what were you leaving London for?

definitions.text: on M1, what were you leaving London for?
definitions.meaning: the M1 motorway runs from London northwards

explanation.surface: A question about why someone once drove out of London on the M1.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as THE N: the M1 runs north from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning at that past moment, so referring to that time.

clue.text: Belief that ink might be this in thing?

definitions.text: Belief that ink might be this in thing?

parts.words: Belief that ink might be this in thing?
parts.note: belief is THINKING; if the ink in it could not be seen, what remains is THING

explanation.surface: Someone convinced that ink might be the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in thing' looks like a trend; it means 'in THING': THINKING (belief) with its INK unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink that cannot be seen is the spy's trick, and here the letters vanish too.

clue.text: Not too bright, like set lecturer keeps quiet

parts.note: eg, for example, means like

indicators.note: keeps tells us the set and lecturer letters hold the quiet one

parts.note: to gel is to set
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A dim teacher, like a jelly, stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not too bright' sounds like a dull person; it is a paint finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A paint finish with a low sheen, between matt and gloss.

clue.text: Something strategic about plea 21's newly lodged

indicators.note: lodged tells us the plea letters are set inside the others
about tells us the letters of entry 21 are turned around

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, the federal agent

indicators.note: newly means the word plea is made anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tactic over a federal agent's freshly entered plea in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy worked out in advance, a plan for winning.

clue.text: Proper Latin: this among other things

indicators.note: among tells us the Latin word is placed within the others

parts.note: et al, et alia, means and other things
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A list of correct Latin terms, this one among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally right and principled, as proper conduct is.

clue.text: Feature of Inquisitor? Try clue requiring modifiation

indicators.note: requiring modification says the words Try clue must be changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter for the Inquisitor puzzle tests a clue that needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inquisitor is a hard puzzle in the i newspaper; 'modifiation' is printed with a letter missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Torturers of the Spanish Inquisition were known for their savagery.

clue.text: Fed whipped cream and gin but no fried rice

indicators.note: whipped suggests a cream beaten up, its letters stirred
fried suggests cooked rice, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone given a meal of whipped cream and gin instead of fried rice.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CREAM and GIN, minus the letters of RICE ('but no fried rice'), to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fed is an American FBI agent, a government man.

clue.text: Hats off to Hobart series that's accounted for boomerang?

indicators.note: the hats are the heads of the following words, taken off them

parts.note: rows are series, lines of things
a tick marks an item as checked and accounted for

explanation.surface: A salute to a Tasmanian cricket series that has been decided.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobart is in Tasmania, Australia, which fits the boomerang.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is an example of a hurled hunting stick.

clue.text: Greeting between two people who act strangely

indicators.note: strangely suggests the words who act behave oddly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two oddly behaving people say hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery informal hello in London slang, a corruption of 'what cheer'.

clue.text: Agreeing to differ isn't the last you'll see of Mike Pence

indicators.note: to differ means the letters of isn't are made different, rearranged
the last you'll see of picks the final letter of Mike

explanation.surface: An agreement to disagree won't be the end of Mike Pence, the US vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreeing to differ' looks like one phrase; 'to differ' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in step is to move in harmony, so to agree.

clue.text: I make God set about New Testament to name…

indicators.note: about tells us the god-making word goes round the testament letters

parts.note: to deify is to make a god of

explanation.surface: A boast about making a god from the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain this clue to the next two, part of the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify is to pick out and name someone or something.

clue.text: Order to be delivered to Head of MI6

parts.note: a parcel marked for someone is to be delivered to them

indicators.note: Head of picks the first letter of MI6

explanation.surface: Instructions to send something to the chief of British intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence service, whose head is known as M in fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Order in the sense of arrangement or shape, as in good form.

clue.text: … possible sources of quicksilver writer …

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury, also called quicksilver
wells are sources, as of water or oil

explanation.surface: A list of where mercury might be found, and an author.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue chained by ellipses; the writer is the author of The Time Machine and The Invisible Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The English author of early science fiction novels.

clue.text: … this person occupying a throne corruptly — Macbeth, say?

indicators.note: occupying tells us the setter sits inside the other letters
corruptly means the words a throne are twisted, rearranged

parts.note: this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: A usurper seizes a throne by foul means, as Macbeth did.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is a central character lacking heroic virtue, an example of the type.

clue.text: Nothing short of evasive on e.g. Dolly's depression

indicators.note: short of says the evasive word goes without the nothing

parts.note: coy means evasive
O, the zero, means nothing
Dolly the sheep is a clone, the first cloned mammal

explanation.surface: A sheep's low mood: Dolly is evasive and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low mood; it is a weather system.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a low-pressure weather system, a meteorological depression.
